title: Humming: backend first, then indexed versus grouped
problem: Marlin currently executes the MXFP4 experts. Backend GEMMs and expert packing can consume different amounts of time for the same routed tokens; EP also affects grouped versus indexed execution.
solution: Compare Marlin, Humming grouped and Humming indexed at identical BF16 activation semantics, routing, transport and graph settings. Use installed controls first; port only missing dispatch behavior.
feasibility: Both audits agree. Fresh adds Humming0.1.16 schema counterevidence and failed #59488 patch application. A selectable name is not proof of legal W1/W2 schemas. Three fixed arms are more informative than bundling backend, activation and precision.
first_check: Record effective backend, W1/W2 schema and GEMM type for both target and draft on every rank. Logs contain E384/top6/local96 and E128/top3/local32 configurations; resolve their role tags and qualify both. Preserve clamp10.
evaluation: Existing E1/E2 plus exact-shape expert/reference fixtures. Measure full routed-expert span including permutation/quantization/combine, HBM/KV loss, accepted tokens and qualified goodput. Static indexed must beat static grouped to support indexed preference.
stop_rule: Stop on illegal schema, silent precision fallback, dispatch mismatch, numerical failure or no useful service improvement. Do not infer a win from GEMM time alone.
b200_transfer: Generic MoE evaluation logic transfers; Blackwell MegaMoE and precision defaults do not. Humming is a particularly concrete Hopper comparator.

title: Share compatible FlashMLA planning metadata
problem: Compatible attention groups can each rebuild the same execution plan during one metadata-building pass, repeating host work and planner launches.
solution: Reuse a plan holder within that pass only when all live compatibility fields match. A tensor-shape match alone is insufficient if lengths, masks or graph buffers differ.
feasibility: Genuinely new to the fresh shortlist: #58818. Its three vLLM source-file changes applied to disposable installed-source copies. No execution, correctness or end-to-end gain was demonstrated.
first_check: Trace active sparse attention builders and count duplicate planner calls plus compatible opportunities. Inspect existing same-type reuse and the holder lifetime. Include target and draft and changing graph replay lengths.
evaluation: E1/E2 remain sufficient for performance. Add shared-versus-separate plan reference tests for ragged lengths, masks, mixed groups, prefill/decode and graph replay. Measure eliminated launches, exposed CPU/planning time and unprofiled TPOT.
stop_rule: Hold if planning is already shared or no compatible duplicates occur. Reject unsafe reuse; mark a tiny effect inconclusive if drift exceeds it.
b200_transfer: Potentially portable orchestration improvement, not a small-head TP4 optimization. No H200 gain follows from H20 synthetic-acceptance results.

title: Use logical requests rather than target padding for drafting
problem: Target CUDA graphs pad requests to a capture capacity. Reusing this padded capacity for DP draft dispatch schedules unnecessary rows, including on lightly loaded/dummy ranks.
solution: Carry real request counts alongside graph capacity and use them coherently in draft inputs, metadata and dispatch, retaining full startup capture capacity.
feasibility: All three audits converge on #58984. Fresh shows source conflicts with the pinned image, so this is an adaptation rather than a demonstrated clean cherry-pick.
first_check: Trace DSpark inheritance into the installed helper; record real, target-padded and draft-padded request counts and every dummy rank. Check equivalent behavior before editing.
evaluation: Use existing E1 and burst/idle-skew E2. Add upstream dummy-rank/distributed fixtures. Compare draft rows/time, collectives, graph mode and ITL at identical acceptance and load.
stop_rule: No eligible excess rows means inactive. Inconsistent per-rank counts or graph-buffer bounds block execution. Padding reduction without service value is a negative serving result.
b200_transfer: The repeated-work mechanism transfers. Seq128 saturation claims and Blackwell timing do not.

title: Reduce CPU DP metadata synchronization overhead
problem: Tiny CPU reductions can delay dispatch even when GPU compute and GPU collectives are fast. Time waiting for late ranks can look like slow transport.
solution: Use the reviewed low-latency CPU reduction implementation only for compatible groups and message ordering; preserve fallback and failure behavior.
feasibility: All three identify #61767. Fresh finds patch conflicts and exposes group-local rank/tag/order checks. Two local DP4 groups differ from the source multi-node benchmarks.
first_check: Measure arrival skew separately from time after the last rank arrives. Attest actual process-group backend, ranks, tensor shape, tags and sequence of calls.
evaluation: E1/E2 plus upstream collective tests and CPU spans. Track scheduler-to-GPU gaps, all-rank progress, collective cost, TTFT/TPOT tails and qualified goodput.
stop_rule: Defer if skew dominates or reduction cost is hidden. Reject ordering/deadlock failures or worse end-to-end tails.
b200_transfer: Hardware-independent CPU logic may transfer, but topology and NUMA determine actual benefit.

title: Tune SM90 mHC for actual one-to-eight-row launches
problem: The repeated fused mHC post/pre-norm kernel uses a launch split tuned for Blackwell. Hopper can prefer a different split at tiny row counts.
solution: Apply #61461 only for SM90 and rows1–8, preserving other shapes and math except documented reduction order.
feasibility: Fresh confirms source hunks apply. Both H200 runs cite H20 evidence; neither measured H200. k5 suggests six logical rows for one request, but graph padding can exceed the gate.
first_check: Count actual executed delayed5120-wide kernel rows, not client concurrency. Resolve the active prenorm binary and qualify the relevant DeepGEMM448/59129 lifetime fix first if executed.
evaluation: Existing client at node concurrency1/2/8 plus normal E1/E2; upstream numerical tests. Track eligible-row fraction, mHC microseconds and low-load TPOT. Treat saturation as a separate endpoint.
stop_rule: Do not rank as a broad capacity win without exposure. A small kernel gain can be beneath server noise; no global benefit if most calls have >8 rows.
b200_transfer: Architecture-specific tuning changes. B200 parameters are precisely what must not be assumed optimal on H200.

title: Repair demonstrated prefix-cache/draft interactions
problem: A target prefix hit may be vetoed by draft-group bookkeeping or expose draft context whose KV was not written. Junction handling can lose reachable sibling prefixes.
solution: Select one matching fix among #47926/#62278/#57110 and related annotations only after distinguishing invalid restored draft context from target-hit loss.
feasibility: Earlier H200/B200 work covers this more explicitly than fresh17. Prefix cache and DSpark are active; symptoms and exact missing behavior remain unmeasured.
first_check: Correlate cached token counts per group, final DP rank, hit length, unaligned boundaries and acceptance. APC-off/cold/warm controls distinguish cache bugs from general drafter weakness.
evaluation: Reuse agent-f75 and cache-heavy Mooncake. Add small same-client sibling/unaligned-prefix fixtures only when absent from the trace. Track recomputed prefill, acceptance, TTFT and reference quality.
stop_rule: Do not cherry-pick a bundle or treat higher acceptance alone as correctness. Hold if equivalent fixes already exist or no specific symptom appears.
b200_transfer: Generic cache/drafter semantics transfer, but V4 flags and other-model evidence need V4.1 inspection.

title: Remove repeated scheduler cache work
problem: Long SWA block tables have large null heads; unchanged partial-prefix boundaries can be registered repeatedly in Python before GPU work starts.
solution: Test #61724 null-head skipping separately from #51333 registration memoization; preserve promotion, copy-on-write, release and preemption invalidation.
feasibility: Retain from earlier audit. Fresh omission is not rejection. Seq64 and H200 GPU costs may leave less exposed CPU time than the B200 high-concurrency source case.
first_check: CPU sample the actual scheduler; count scanned null entries and repeat registrations at identical block/hash. Verify missing implementation.
evaluation: E1/E2 with long-context cohorts and CPU spans; upstream cache lifecycle tests. Measure GPU idle gaps and useful end-to-end improvement.
stop_rule: No measured repeated work or hidden CPU cost means defer. Cache lifetime regressions reject the patch.
b200_transfer: Code-level mechanism transfers; source percentages from roughly900 running requests do not.

title: Hopper selector integration and length-aware block selection
problem: The installed selector gates DeepSelect to SM100; candidate-block selection can scan max-context-width padding instead of only valid blocks.
solution: First qualify SM90 native DeepSelect with the correct FP32/stride contract. Then isolate #61039 valid-length selection from the selector replacement. These are distinct factors.
feasibility: Fresh #59204 Python hunks apply, but native compilation/tests were excluded from that check. Earlier H200 correctly identifies #61039 cannot deliver its intended Hopper path merely by changing Python.
first_check: Resolve extension revision/build target, actual dtype/K/width/alignment, valid counts and loaded binary. Test actual width rather than equating prompt tokens with compressed logit columns.
evaluation: E1 short live contexts under large max context diagnose padded work; E2 covers ragged cases. Upstream top-k bounds/ties/NaN and changed-input graph tests; compare selector-only, then length-aware.
stop_rule: Do not confuse this with candidate-only decode scoring C09. No native support or mismatched numerical/ordering contract blocks execution.
b200_transfer: B200 can access different native selector paths; the same PR ID does not imply equal integration effort on Hopper.

title: Candidate-only long-context decode scoring
problem: Dense Hopper decode indexing can score the full compressed context even though only a candidate subset will be consumed.
solution: Compare dense scoring with #62000 candidate-K gathering and #62463 direct paged-K scoring as separate alternatives, keeping selection semantics and prefill unchanged.
feasibility: Both H200 audits converge. Fresh shows both patches conflict with installed code; #62000 reports a single-request regression. Neither author result proves current H200 value.
first_check: Match FP8 cache format, compressed row IDs, causal bounds and candidate producer. Count candidates versus full live columns; configured pool2048×8 is not automatically the number used on every request.
evaluation: Inspect Mooncake length histogram before adding a new cohort. Existing client can extend32K/128K and feasible longer lengths if needed. Measure bytes, gather/temp cost, score/selection agreement and context-stratified ITL, including short/C1 controls.
stop_rule: If candidate setup costs exceed avoided dense work, keep dense fallback. Fixed8K E1 alone cannot establish a long-context frontier improvement.
b200_transfer: Earlier B200 E01 length-aware block selection is related, not the same algorithm; do not count them as repeated independent confirmation.

title: Preserve cache affinity at the final DP rank
problem: Endpoint affinity can be lost when separate API workers choose different internal DP ranks, scattering warm prefixes.
solution: Use load-aware internal prefix tie-breaking (#52464), retaining salt isolation and load precedence. Shared frontend state is a distinct expansion beyond a local tie-break.
feasibility: All three contain the idea; source high-load effects are weak/mixed. Actual router source differs between baseline snapshots and must be reconciled.
first_check: Join request, endpoint, API PID and final rank. Show locality loss at the internal selector and absent equivalent affinity before implementation.
evaluation: Existing E1 prefix pools and E2 cache-heavy/burst. Measure token-weighted hit rate, queue skew, CPU overhead and TTFT tails; hold out new sessions and heavy imbalance.
stop_rule: Reject stale/unsafe shared state or worsened tails. Affinity that only improves idle C1 does not establish saturation throughput value.
b200_transfer: Generic routing idea transfers; different router source/settings can entirely change the apparent opportunity.

title: Bound coordinated DP prefill release
problem: A prefill-heavy rank can stall decode peers during synchronized steps, producing decode tail spikes.
solution: Compare existing scheduling with one of #51199/#61834, separately. Freeze a bounded policy after discovery; preserve dummy/pause/cancel participation.
feasibility: Shared lead across all audits. A check performed only when a step starts does not guarantee a hard wall-clock waiting bound during long steps.
first_check: Measure mixed-step interference and oldest-prefill age. Inspect starvation escape, long-step timing and interaction with existing prefill interval controls.
evaluation: E1 and E2 burst/mixed loads plus distributed lifecycle fixtures. Track TTFT and TPOT together, per-rank backlog, accepted tokens/step and collective wait.
stop_rule: Reject decode gains bought with violated prefill SLOs or deadlocks. Do not interpret fixed steps as fixed emitted tokens under DSpark.
b200_transfer: Scheduling mechanism transfers, but slower/faster prefill and communication change the useful policy.

title: Contiguous prefill MQA epilogue
problem: The contiguous SM90 MQA logits epilogue can spend instructions on ReLU that a different arithmetic form may reduce.
solution: Evaluate DeepGEMM452 at identical compile/launch settings, with an enforceable numerical domain or stock fallback. Paged decode is unchanged.
feasibility: Fresh strengthens earlier H16: installed header is old, but loaded JIT artifact remains unproved. Saved CPU counterexample disproves universal finite-input equivalence, not actual deployment correctness.
first_check: Trace actual contiguous prefill calls, FP8/BF16 API and logit dtype, loaded header/JIT binary and input/scale ranges. Positive x near FLT_MAX can overflow in x+abs(x) before later compensation.
evaluation: Existing uncached/mixed prefill E1/E2; warm-prefix and paged-only negative controls. Add extreme/real-range, scale-underflow, tie/top-k and quality references. Compare full prefill TTFT, not best-of-three kernel time.
stop_rule: No defendable bounds or reference mismatch blocks the arithmetic change. An extreme CPU counterexample alone does not prove real H200 model failure.
b200_transfer: Hardware-specific Hopper kernel lead; do not attribute any decode gain to this prefill-only epilogue.

title: Per-token FP8 Humming activation
problem: Activation format can change expert GEMM arithmetic and memory cost, independently of backend choice and indexed/grouped execution.
solution: After C01 establishes a legal incumbent, compare BF16 and explicitly supported per-token FP8 with fixed GEMM/transport; quantify conversion costs and quality.
feasibility: Fresh correctly splits this from backend selection. Humming0.1.16 block-FP8 schema mismatch and MXFP8 limitations cannot be ignored or silently bypassed.
first_check: Attest effective target/draft W1/W2 scales, formats and no fallback. Do not infer that advertised schema acceptance proves a legal SM90 kernel.
evaluation: E1/E2 plus actual generation-quality/reference fixtures because arithmetic changes. Measure quantization+GEMM+combine, acceptance, output quality and KV/workspace cost.
stop_rule: Reject hidden format fallback, unsupported schema, quality regression or no useful combined-span improvement.
b200_transfer: Precision names and native hardware support differ; Blackwell FP4/FP8 choices are not interchangeable Hopper controls.

title: Fuse top-k with physical KV-slot mapping
problem: After selection, index IDs may be converted to physical KV slots in separate launches, creating temporary traffic and synchronization.
solution: For consumers needing only physical slots, fuse mapping into selection. Preserve raw-ID paths and ordering for consumers that still need logical positions.
feasibility: Fresh cross-engine extension (SGLang41561); also inspect FlashInfer5889/current vLLM equivalents before custom implementation. Torch-chain microbench is not the strongest comparator.
first_check: Trace all consumers, block64 mapping, causal/order/tie contracts and native SM90 operator. Compare to C08 selector-only with identical selected sets.
evaluation: Three arms: current chain, fast selector+separate mapping, fast selector+fused mapping. Same E1/E2 plus raw-ID fallback, page-reuse and changed-length graph correctness.
stop_rule: If raw IDs are still needed, saved traffic may disappear. Do not attribute fast-selector gains to mapping fusion.
b200_transfer: Transfer concept from another engine, not a drop-in PR; existing vLLM implementation must be checked.

title: Shared Engram placement and exposed lookup cost
problem: CPU-offloaded lookup cost may depend on shared physical backing, NUMA placement and translation behavior even when private allocation waste is absent.
solution: Keep current shared ownership. First compare supported NUMA-local placement/settings; only then consider separately scoped shared-cuMem or lookup-threshold changes.
feasibility: Fresh proves dp_shared_memory=True on both replicas. Earlier H10 included multiple arms: its private exact-allocation arm is inactive, but shared placement is not disproven. dp_shared_memory does not identify physical backing by itself.
first_check: Inspect /dev/shm versus cuMem, physical PSS, registration/page type, allocation NUMA and exposed lookup spans. Probe FABRIC/export support before proposing a shared-cuMem implementation.
evaluation: Reuse E1/E2 with host memory/NUMA/lookup counters. Keep sorting and placement isolated; compare lookup span and end-to-end prefill, not summed RSS of shared mappings.
stop_rule: No active allocation delta or fully hidden lookup cost means hold. Host-memory savings alone do not free GPU KV or lower node price.
b200_transfer: GB200 coherent-memory/page-walk thresholds are not H200 defaults. Requires a new shared-storage scope rather than reviving the rejected private card.

title: Scheduler budget reserved for separate drafts
problem: Charging separate DSpark draft slots against target scheduling can reduce usable work when the token budget is tight.
solution: Compare #59468 at unchanged seq64/MBT16384/k5 only when actual budget-bound steps are observed.
feasibility: Earlier audit retains this; fresh top17 omits it. At this large budget, source MBT512 gains are a weak transfer. Prefill can still consume budget, so not a mathematical proof of inactivity.
first_check: Measure charged versus scheduled target tokens and requests blocked by budget, separating prefill pressure and buffers.
evaluation: E1/E2 and upstream buffer-bound tests. Preserve MBT; a smaller-budget synthetic diagnostic is labelled separately.
stop_rule: Do not lower MBT merely to manufacture a baseline benefit. No binding resource means defer.
b200_transfer: Generic scheduler logic transfers; original bottleneck severity does not.

title: Unreachable draft graph buckets
problem: Rounding target-derived capture sizes to draft query length can omit an otherwise legal full draft batch.
solution: Apply #62040 boundary correction only if an actual missing bucket or eager fallback is demonstrated.
feasibility: Both H200 audits reject carrying seq128×6 pressure unchanged: target384 and draft320 fit cap512 at seq64. Capacity coverage alone still does not prove every intermediate bucket exists.
first_check: Enumerate actual target/draft capture ladders and observe selected bucket/eager fraction at live shapes.
evaluation: Existing E1/E2 and boundary tests; record launch overhead, graph HBM and remaining KV blocks.
stop_rule: No missing live bucket means no-op. Do not increase graph cap blindly and consume KV headroom.
b200_transfer: B200 benchmark seq128 differs from H200 seq64; a launch-configuration diagnosis is not an architecture-independent fact.

title: Bound drafter context if long-context acceptance collapses
problem: Draft attention cost or acceptance can deteriorate outside a drafter-compatible context range.
solution: Test #61261 bounded window only after separating length effects from prefix-restoration bugs and workload domain. Adaptive verification stays off.
feasibility: Earlier audit retains this; absence from fresh17 is not a refutation. Current evidence comes from another model/hardware.
first_check: Measure draft time and accepted length versus actual context, hit state and content; inspect drafter training context/RoPE.
evaluation: Existing long-context/session/Mooncake cohorts and cached real-domain SPEEDBench if necessary. Keep short-context control and task quality.
stop_rule: No length-dependent problem means hold. Acceptance gain with quality or throughput loss does not support serving value.
b200_transfer: Concept may transfer; the original Kimi evidence does not validate DeepSeek.

title: Native MXFP4 SM90 fused expert backend
problem: Separate expert dispatch, staging, GEMM and combine can expose more time than a compatible fused implementation.
solution: Compare FlashInfer6343/6517 and DeepGEMM411/473 eligibility before writing an adapter. Keep native MXFP4 semantics and required activation clamp; use a dependency-matched unfused control.
feasibility: Fresh materially improves old X02 with native-MXFP4 leads. vLLM62603 is block-FP8, not a ready native-MXFP4 adapter. Current FlashInfer0.7.0.post1 may lack required APIs.
first_check: Prove E384/top6/local96 AND E128/top3/local32 routing branches, H5120/I2304, clamp10, nibble order, scale ranges, EP4 workspace agreement, empty ranks and graph lifetimes.
evaluation: Kernel/reference and distributed correctness before E1/E2. Measure fused expert span plus workspace/KV loss and quality. If precision changes, label combined backend/precision effect instead of pure fusion.
stop_rule: Stop unsupported semantics before spending on serving builds. EP8 push-dispatch source gains do not predict EP4.
b200_transfer: Blackwell integrated MegaMoE is an active incumbent there; Hopper requires separate integration, so priority and cost change sharply.

title: DeepEP activation, then triple-buffer dispatch
problem: Direct-NVLink dispatch may benefit from overlapping hidden/scales/metadata movement, but the current allgather/reducescatter path never executes that DeepEP kernel.
solution: Stage1: compatible fixed DeepEP versus current AG/RS. Stage2: DeepEP baseline versus #693 triple buffering, with combine unchanged.
feasibility: Fresh-only explicit design. H100 direct-NVLink evidence and later elastic API changes require version-matched adapter work.
first_check: Check EP4 payload/scales, routing ranks, shared-memory/workspace limits, direct path eligibility and exact adapter API. Require independent idle/zero-token collective participation.
evaluation: E1/E2 with skew and mixed loads; measure dispatch AND combine, queue/compute overlap and memory/KV cost. Isolate activation from the kernel patch.
stop_rule: No active compatible DeepEP path means the patch is inapplicable; a changed backend gain does not validate triple buffering.
b200_transfer: Communication concepts transfer but actual selected backend and EP topology govern eligibility.

title: SM90 mHC coefficient overlap
problem: Coefficient work may run concurrently with another stage if dependencies and GPU resources permit useful overlap.
solution: Opt in to #60768 on SM90 after qualifying affected prenorm synchronization. Keep TF32 overlap separate from compensated-BF16 primitives.
feasibility: Both H200 runs retain as exploratory; old installed gate is SM100. Draft proposal has no target serving validation.
first_check: Trace executed JIT artifact, event/stream dependencies and resource occupancy; first resolve DeepGEMM448/vLLM59129 applicability.
evaluation: Reference/repeatability and changed-input graph fixtures; short Nsight timeline separate from unprofiled E1/E2. Measure exposed critical path, not merely concurrent kernel bars.
stop_rule: Overlap that slows both kernels or introduces races is rejected. CPU tests do not establish GPU lifetime safety.
b200_transfer: SM100 fused-allreduce overlap implementation cannot simply be enabled on SM90.

title: KV offload as a separate capacity configuration
problem: Cache eviction may force repeated prefill; external KV capacity helps only when avoided recomputation exceeds transfer and management costs.
solution: Activate one compatible connector as a separate baseline, then test matching save/restore fixes individually.
feasibility: Not enabled in the observed commands. Engram CPU offload and Mooncake trace replay do not imply KV offload is active.
first_check: Prove reuse beyond GPU capacity and resolve draft-group ownership, transport and host budget. Verify each connector prerequisite and restore lifetime.
evaluation: Existing cache-heavy replay plus narrow eviction/restore/cancel/stale-KV fixtures. Measure hit-source tokens, transfers, acceptance, TTFT and physical memory.
stop_rule: No pressure/benefit means hold. Wrong restored KV or transfer-induced tail failure vetoes the path.
b200_transfer: Generic capacity tradeoff, but H200 memory and transfer costs change the crossover.

title: Matched SGLang control
problem: A different serving engine may expose an achievable service gap, but engine-level differences bundle many mechanisms.
solution: Match checkpoint/tokenizer, TP1/DP4/EP4, host Engram, KV precision, graph/cache settings and actual DSpark rejection. Then isolate any group32 tuning within SGLang separately.
feasibility: Fresh adds a useful external comparator. It is not a vLLM-fork patch and should not displace cheap first experiments.
first_check: Produce a parity checklist with irreducible differences, including tool encoding, target/drafter math, sampling and output counts.
evaluation: Same frozen E1/E2 and quality gates; report unmatched factors. A matched engine gap motivates investigation, not attribution to a single kernel.
stop_rule: No semantic parity means report an informative but confounded comparison, not a valid A/B for one PR.
b200_transfer: Source H200 bundle headlines cannot be decomposed into additive vLLM patch gains.

title: Private Engram exact allocation: inactive
problem: The exact-registration proposal targets rounded private tables.
solution: No live change proposed: preserve the historical card and reject its private-path applicability; use separately scoped C15 for shared storage.
feasibility: Fresh resolved logs prove dp_shared_memory=True for both replicas. That meets the private card's own rejection condition.
first_check: Reopen only if a future baseline actually uses private rounded allocations.
evaluation: No GPU experiment needed for an inactive branch. Retain the evidence in the decision ledger.
stop_rule: Do not call all Engram work disproven; only this allocation intervention is inactive.
b200_transfer: Original GB10/B200 private allocation evidence is not this deployed branch.

title: TP4 Marlin alignment alternative
problem: TP4 expert width576 pads to640 at128 alignment;64 alignment avoids that padding.
solution: Only evaluate #56697 against a separately qualified TP4 baseline.
feasibility: Current TP1/EP4 width2304 is already128-aligned, so this mechanism is inactive.
first_check: User must deliberately select a TP topology study; do not mix a topology switch with the patch effect.
evaluation: Same E1/E2 with TP4-specific memory/quality checks and standalone baseline.
stop_rule: No padding difference at live TP1 means no live patch gain.
b200_transfer: Shape arithmetic, not GPU brand alone, determines applicability.

title: Small-head sparse attention alternative
problem: Padding8/16/32 local attention heads to64 can waste work.
solution: Native-head prefill #61615 and decode #59418, or alternative #57673, only on eligible local-head shapes.
feasibility: TP1 retains64 heads; live configuration does not match. TP4 gives16, a different experiment.
first_check: Confirm local heads and actual query rows; resolve FlashMLA26 dependency.
evaluation: Separate TP4 E1/E2 plus numerical attention references; alternatives isolated.
stop_rule: No small-head shape means inactive on the requested deployment.
b200_transfer: Architecture-specific backend support and topology both matter.

title: TP-sharded fused prefill projection
problem: Replicated TP projection can duplicate work at sufficiently large prefill batches.
solution: Shard rows and all-gather via #58872 only when TP>1 and break-even is measured.
feasibility: TP1 has no cross-TP redundancy; H20-derived H200 thresholds are unmeasured.
first_check: Separate TP4 baseline and compatible collective/SP/LoRA checks.
evaluation: Prefill E1/E2, projection plus gather timing, numerical references.
stop_rule: No TP redundancy means no current benefit.
b200_transfer: Do not extrapolate a TP4 optimization to DP4.

title: Blackwell MegaMoE warmup and activation repacking
problem: First-use compilation and redundant activation packing can waste time on particular MegaMoE paths.
solution: Retain B200 designs; reopen only for the exact equivalent active Hopper backend.
feasibility: Current H200 Marlin/AGRS does not establish the Blackwell MegaMoE call path. Cold-start time is also distinct from warm serving capacity.
first_check: Find matching symbols/dtypes in an actually selected H200 route before porting any PR.
evaluation: If active later, independent startup or packing diagnostics plus E1/E2, appropriate to the claim.
stop_rule: Hardware-tag keywords do not prove a generic fix irrelevant, but no active equivalent path means no recommendation.
b200_transfer: B200 E05/E08 priorities cannot be inherited unchanged.

title: B200 FlashMLA pipeline and Engram/mHC fusion
problem: The B200-specific FlashMLA pipeline and Blackwell-only TP1 fusion target unavailable SM100 behavior.
solution: Retain as B200 work; a real SM90 adaptation would be a new scoped proposal.
feasibility: TP1 matching alone does not bypass the Blackwell gate in #60938.
first_check: Require an actual Hopper implementation and correctness evidence before reopening.
evaluation: No current H200 experiment from a mere flag change.
stop_rule: Do not silently remove architecture guards.
b200_transfer: These are major examples of why copying the B200 rank would be wrong.

title: Sampling distribution qualification
problem: Reused random draws across block-verification rounds can bias generation despite normal acceptance and throughput.
solution: Qualify #61161/equivalent implementation on the actual stochastic path.
feasibility: Probabilistic DSpark/block rejection is configured; source membership and executed path still matter.
first_check: Use upstream analytical target/draft fixture and independent seeds/temperatures.
evaluation: Distribution tests with predeclared tolerance and comparisons; temperature0 E1 cannot prove this property.
stop_rule: A sampling failure blocks affected performance comparisons; no speedup is claimed.
b200_transfer: Semantic correctness transfers; image membership must be checked.

title: Index/graph bounds and mHC lifetime qualification
problem: Invalid top-k tail lanes, graph state or asynchronous operand lifetime can silently corrupt results.
solution: Map each active H200 kernel to its relevant fix, especially62467 and DeepGEMM448/59129; retain Blackwell-only barrier checks in B200 scope.
feasibility: Fresh source shows affected TF32 header ordering, but executed JIT/binary must be resolved. Source presence is not observed corruption.
first_check: Identify exact dispatch, dependency binary and changed-input graph/tail/empty-row cases.
evaluation: Upstream references, replay/repeatability and bounded sanitizer cases for changed paths; no unrelated universal test quota.
stop_rule: Do not claim a slow/fast candidate is valid before this scope passes.
b200_transfer: B200 G03 SM100 mega_mhc barrier fix is not identical to Hopper WGMMA lifetime fix.

title: API2 liveness and restart identity
problem: DP wake-up ordering and draft compile-cache identity can fail during idle/resume or cached restart.
solution: Qualify #59559 and #62062 only when the specific coordinated/independent DP semantics match.
feasibility: API2 is present; #62062 dense independent DP evidence is not automatically coordinated EP4 proof.
first_check: Inspect data_parallel_index and pause/wave transitions on a test deployment.
evaluation: Small lifecycle fixtures; steady E1/E2 alone do not cover them.
stop_rule: No restart of user services performed during this comparison.
b200_transfer: Generic lifecycle concerns transfer, exact DP mode determines each fix.

title: Tool encoding, parser and changed-math quality
problem: Fast token output can hide malformed tool encodings/streams or degraded task quality after precision/engine changes.
solution: Freeze intended checkpoint encoding, use reference tool-role fixtures and evaluate changed-math quality with a pinned suitable suite.
feasibility: DeepSeek v41 parser is active; encoder upgrades change input token counts and must become a common qualified control.
first_check: Check #62199/#62259/equivalent behavior and actual tokenizer revision.
evaluation: Golden token IDs/JSON stream assembly plus quality only where math/engine changes warrant it. Synthetic text sessions are insufficient for actual tool-role semantics.
stop_rule: Correctness/quality regression vetoes affected serving promotion.
b200_transfer: Same checks across hardware, while deployed revisions may differ.
